source_text: So, I minted you codex-33 to use.  Your analysis above sounds quite nice, very rigorous. The informal additions that I can make are that #1 we reprise the causal story inside of each pattern in terms of its BECAUSE, so I think even one pattern should be readable in terms of our 3 stories. There are tokens that it accepts and emits, e.g. something either is or is not an ALCOVE to use Alexander's example.  And you could build a house with lots and lots of ALCOVEs in it, but it would not actually be that nice (this is an Alexander / Salingaros treatment of what we could subsequently treat in free energy terms).  And, lastly, it is a blend at a primordial level and the "held tension" is the emergent structure.  So, my point is, each pattern is itself a tiny diamond, and the composition in a cascade includes that inner structure and any outer structure (like your outer-loop-diamond example).  Indeed, we could probably say: in the case in which we produce a cascade that can reduce to a diamond we can restate it as a design pattern.  #2. The *informal proof* story.  There are lots of examples; but just think of the War Machine itself as an example.  I don't remember exactly how many iterations there were, but each adds new structure and more explicit requirements; sometimes these are "additional requirements" and sometimes they are just "better structure".  In the case in which its "better structure" we are refining something like Alexander's street corner.  It still has a newstand and a greengrocer and a crosswalk or whatever, but now it also has a fire hydrant, a manhole, etc.  In fact, there is the most lovely example I can tell you about: it's R Crumb's picture of a crossing street in America over the years.  Not only does the object itself get refined as we add detail, the "object" is a living object that changes over time.

Running. Now the Lean receipt.㊥ (gist) Both of your additions are in the note (futon2 `039844a13`), check 2 is done in Lean (mathlib4 `e5fa4352a5`), and check 1 is running on codex-33. The pattern-as-diamond reading turned out to give something concrete at once: the outer-loop diamond restates as a single flexiarg whose HOWEVER is literally the held tension already written in `injury-routes-to-self-heal`, and the "house of alcoves" is the off-diagonal claude-17's compiler does not yet charge.

㊢ ("each pattern is itself a tiny diamond") Written as a table in §2a: IF/context = the generic space and the tokens accepted; HOWEVER = the two input spaces, the forces in conflict; THEN = the blend, whose emergent structure is the held tension (an alcove is neither the family room nor a private room) and the token emitted (is / is not an ALCOVE); BECAUSE = why the square commutes, the pattern's own structural equation that `k-unmet = k-if ∧ ¬k-then` abstracts. IF on top, two forces incomparable, THEN their meet — so a pattern is a blend square and a four-node semilattice at once, and a cascade is diamonds pasted along tokens, the same shape at two grains.

㊟ ("lots and lots of ALCOVEs … not actually be that nice") In claude-17's terms that is the *other* off-diagonal: `IF ∧ ¬THEN` is a problem unaddressed, which he counts; `¬IF ∧ THEN` is a solution without its problem, which nobody counts. A per-step C that credits tokens held rewards exactly this (it is §5's bag problem at the grain of one pattern); the token story handles it the way v2 handles a missing edge — an emitted token with no consuming want earns nothing. Both off-diagonals should cost; today only one does.

㊢ ("we could probably say … restate it as a design pattern") The outer-loop diamond is the instance: IF = `observe`; HOWEVER = ordinary work against self-repair, which is word for word `injury`'s HOWEVER ("merely adding a large penalty to M/E/T leaves unsafe acts in support … treating every failure as injury creates a self-repair dark room"); THEN = `minimise`; BECAUSE = G is defined over policies with predicted consequences. A complete flexiarg, `meta/select-the-meta-item`, drafted in the note and not put in the library — that is yours.

🈖 ("additional requirements" / "better structure") My reading, in §5a: two moves on the diagram. An additional requirement pastes in a new square (new want token, new input space); better structure replaces a blend by one higher in Goguen's quality order over the same inputs — the 3/2-pushout is the maximum among consistent cones, refinement is movement toward it, and a living object (Crumb's crossroads) is one whose inputs also move, so the maximum moves. First classification of our own record: 09-15 → v2 and v2 → v3 are better structure over the same wants; Q1–Q10 and the pattern-graph diff were additional requirements. Checkable against the spec history, after the §6 items.

㊬ (check 2, Lean) `ConstructionReceipt.lean` now carries the diamond: four units, four token-carrying edges, meet witness (fill, injury) → minimise. `diamondReceipt_valid` and `diamondReceiptInjuryFirst_valid` — the two linear extensions over one support, the two parses of one formation — both `true`; `chainReceipt_invalid` and `chainReceiptForgedToken_invalid` — the recipe's fill → injury step as an edge, with an empty token set or a forged one — both `false`, since `produces fill ∩ needs injury = ∅`. `lake build DarkTower.WarMachine.ConstructionReceipt`: 584 jobs, success; all five by `native_decide`.

previous_reply_acts.text: (gist) I took the outer-loop cascade as the real example and read it three ways on run c9d25d6a's record. The note is `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/NOTE-outer-cascade-as-pasted-blends-2026-10-05.md` (futon2 `1f2bd525d`), no code touched and daxiang_live untouched. Short version: the outer cascade already exists as a diamond of four meta patterns whose precedence set *is* a semilattice, the blend reading derives that diamond from what the four patterns share, the token reading makes it the first non-toy `ConstructionReceipt`, and the causal reading shows that the click performed one of its four patterns. Your "parametric in the META item" has a clean statement in Goguen's terms, and so does the circumstance under which structure must change.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("ONE cascade from the outer loop") There are two outer loops. `futon3/library/meta/meta-outer-policy-cascade.edn` (2 Oct) is the diamond: observe → {fill, injury} → minimise, four edges, two linear extensions, six typed slots, argmin-G, boundary `:produces :selected-meta-policy`. Its evaluator `meta_outer_policy.clj` is called by nothing in the click. What the click runs is `meta_live_outer_selector` → `meta_pipeline_selector/select` over Cascade Live: on c9d25d6a it excluded 569 of 676 items (506 off the current map), ranked 107 by a pairwise sum of cost channels, and selected `M-interim-director-proxy-metric-inventory` because its centrality cost `1/(1+33)` was lowest; `:epistemic-value-nats 0.0`, no injury observation, no outer-policy receipt. So the META item was chosen by a centrality ranking, not by the cascade.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("minimizing G *doesn't* mean changing the cascade structurally") In 3/2 terms: the tactical loop constructs the *diagram* per problem and G orders diagrams; the outer loop fixes the diagram and G orders the *cones* over minimise's square — each filled candidate is a consistent cone over (admitted family, generative model, shared outcome vocabulary), and Goguen's "two different 3/2-pushouts need not be isomorphic" is precisely two META items being different blends of the same inputs. The target slot is the parameter; the squares do not move.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("we really do need to change it structurally depending on circumstances") Structure must change exactly when the fixed diagram has no non-degenerate cone: a required slot unfillable from HEAD (the record shows the shape — `declared-priority-cost` filled for 0 of 107, freshness for 79), a singleton family, or injury with no matching A item. In the first case a *reading* square (your 25 Sept read-criteria / ask / defer steps, with epistemic value when the fact is absent) gets pasted in before `fill`. So: four fixed squares plus a fifth under a stated absence, and which absence can be read from the record rather than guessed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (bringing the three stories together) Blend: each meta pattern's I₁, I₂, G, B read off its own text (table in §2 of the note); observe's B is an input of both fill and injury, which is why they are incomparable and one frontier, and fill's and injury's Bs are minimise's two inputs, which is why minimise is their meet. Tokens: the same four edges carry `{field-observation}`, `{field-observation, injury-observation}`, `{filled-candidates, typed-exclusions}`, `{admitted-support, rearm-slot}` — the gluing object of the blend reading and the token of the receipt are one thing seen from two sides, which was the bridge v3 §3 left open. Causal: with claude-17's compiler unchanged and link theories running down the diamond instead of up the `@why` cone, the c9d25d6a record reads as observe partly met, fill unmet, injury unobserved, minimise unmet — his §9 item 3 applied to a click.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("a cascade is more efficient than a flat list … haven't proved … than a chain") In the code the list and the chain are one object: the list kernel fires one pattern per step in order. So the two measurements we have (30 Sept: chain 3.0749 vs one-edge 1.4147; 5 Oct: list 10.715 vs frontier 9.465) are already cascade-versus-chain, both under a per-step C, neither with formation cost. What is unmeasured is the bag, and there v2's "a missing edge is not simultaneous success" has to enter the score first or the bag wins for free. Formation cost as accounting: forming the chain = forming the cascade + choosing a linear extension, log₂(#extensions) bits (one for the diamond) and no token — that is your "recipe is strictly additional work" and "a proof is not a tree", made countable, not yet measured.
